name: x509-parse-chain
algorithm: std.x509 Parse alone of three DER certificates (std/x509/testdata's chain and root, decoded from hex at run time), <reps> passes, the checksum the sum of (NotBefore + NotAfter) mod 1000 in Unix seconds (mk/x509-parse-chain.mk). No signature is checked: the row measures std.x509's own share, which x509-verify-chain's two ECDSA verifications hide.

skip.c: no std X.509: C has no standard certificate library (OpenSSL is third-party)
skip.rust: no std X.509: Rust std has none; x509-parser and rustls-webpki are third-party, and no crate stands in (plan/06-m6.md 4.1)

notes: Work per certificate: Mk x509.Parse (one pass over std.encoding's DER reader, every extension std.x509 uses validated as Go validates it, no allocation, the arena reset per pass); Go crypto/x509 ParseCertificate (allocating, every extension and the public key parsed); Zig 0.17.0 std.crypto.Certificate.parse (the TBS fields' places, the validity, the subjectAltName's place; no extension validation and no key parse, so it does less than the other two).
Checksums computed from the fixtures' validity (2000-01-01 and 2200-01-01 for all three). Written by the std-x509 lane; publish is the bench lane's.

Causes of Mk's ratio against Zig (D-673, D-798): the call into std.encoding's DerRead per element, which D8-7's one DER reader keeps, then the name and extension validation Zig's parse does not do (std-x509's smoke cuts, D-798; not a tools/bench measurement).
